tex_content.label: thm:three-shrinkers
tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Classification retaining the given flow] An admissible three-dimensional static shrinking soliton $(N,h,f)$ with $\lambda =1/2$ generates a shrinking Ricci flow $G(t)$, $t<0$, with $G(-1)=h$. Every supplied shrinking flow associated to these data is, by fixed identifications at all negative times, a compact round flow, a round two-sphere times a line, or a quotient of that product by a free isometric involution. Every three-dimensional asymptotic limit from Theorem 2 has bounded curvature on each slice and such a presentation on its original limit carrier.

↗ thm:surface-ancient Source: MT2007 1. Theorem 9.42, pp. 206–2082. Proposition 9.46, pp. 209–2133. Claim 9.51, p. 2154. Corollaries 9.53–9.54, pp. 217–218↗ lem:ancient-heat-contacts ↗ lem:ancient-singleton-level ↗ lem:ancient-soul-coordinates ↗ lem:ancient-terminal-cylinder ↗ lem:ancient-antipodal-collar
Proof for admissible static data

The soliton potential generates the shrinking flow on the original carrier. The Ricci-nullity maximum principle separates the strictly positive and splitting cases. In the splitting case a parallel line factor leaves a round surface; deck transformations give the product or free involution quotient. In the strictly positive case the potential-level geometry and the surface rigidity estimates force the compact round alternative. Each construction preserves the supplied metric and time-dependent identifications.

□
